items.question_en: When 54 g of ice at −20 °C is mixed with 25 g of steam at 100 °C, then the final mixture at thermal equilibrium contains
options_en: 73 g water at 100 °C and 6 g steam at 100 °C
8 g steam at 100 °C and 12 g water at 0 °C

solution.approach: Find the heat needed to bring all the ice to water at 100°C, then find how much of the steam must condense to supply exactly that heat.

steps.text: Find the heat needed to warm the ice from −20°C to 0°C.
Find the heat needed to melt the ice at 0°C.
Find the heat needed to warm this melted ice from 0°C to 100°C.
Add these to get the total heat needed to bring all 54 g of ice to water at 100°C.
Find the heat released if the full 25 g of steam condenses at 100°C.
steps.why_this_step: Steam gives up heat by condensing to water at the same 100°C before any further cooling can happen.

steps.text: Since the heat available exceeds the heat needed, the ice side reaches 100°C before all the steam condenses, so the final temperature is 100°C and only part of the steam turns to water.
Find the mass of steam that condenses by dividing the heat actually used by the latent heat of vaporisation.
State the final mixture: the condensed steam adds to the melted ice as water, and the rest of the steam remains as steam, both at 100°C.
steps.equation: water = 54 + 19 = 73 g at 100°C; steam left = 25 − 19 = 6 g at 100°C

final_answer.value: 73 g water at 100°C and 6 g steam at 100°C

common_mistakes.text: Assuming all 25 g of steam condenses without checking the heat balance gives 79 g of water at 100°C, a total that matches none of the printed options.
Forgetting that the ice must first warm from −20°C to 0°C before melting, and using only the melting and 0→100°C heat (9720 cal), gives 72 g water and 7 g steam left, matching no option.
